name: Affinity Partners

summary.text: Affinity Partners is a Miami-area private equity firm formed by Jared Kushner in 2021, after he left his post as senior adviser in the first Trump White House. Its debut fund was anchored by a $2 billion commitment from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, with the remainder of its roughly $3 billion from sovereign funds of the UAE and Qatar, Taiwanese businessman Terry Gou and an unnamed investor, according to Senate Finance Committee letters; the firm reported to the SEC that about 99 percent of its capital came from non-U.S. sources. In December 2024 it raised a further $1.5 billion from the Qatar Investment Authority and Abu Dhabi's Lunate. Senate Finance chairman Ron Wyden opened an inquiry into its fees and foreign funding in June 2024; House and Senate Democrats wrote again in March 2026.

facts.claim: Jared Kushner formed Affinity Partners shortly after leaving the White House in January 2021, and by the end of 2021 the firm had raised about $3 billion for a debut fund.
facts.quote: Kushner formed Affinity shortly after leaving the White House, and by the end of 2021 had raised $3 billion for a debut fund.

sources.title: Kushner's fund has reaped millions in fees, but so far returned no profits

facts.claim: According to the Senate Finance Committee chairman's June 2024 letter, Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund committed $2 billion to Affinity in June 2021, and the remaining roughly $1 billion of the firm's capital came from sovereign wealth funds owned by the governments of the United Arab Emirates and Qatar, Taiwanese businessman Terry Gou, and an investor whose identity had not been publicly reported. The letter is a congressional inquiry, not a finding.
facts.quote: a $2 billion investment from the Saudi Public Investment Fund made in June 2021 ... the remaining $1 billion is split between sovereign wealth funds owned by the governments of the United Arab Emirates and Qatar; Terry Gou, a Taiwanese billionaire and politician who is the founder of the world's largest electronics manufacturer; and another investor whose identity has not been publicly reported.

sources.title: Letter from Chairman Wyden to Lauren Key, Chief Financial Officer, A Fin Management LLC

facts.claim: Middle East Eye, relaying New York Times reporting based on previously undisclosed documents, reported that a panel screening investments for the Public Investment Fund objected to the $2 billion commitment to Affinity, citing the 'inexperience' of the fund's management, a proposed asset-management fee it considered 'excessive', and 'public relations risks' arising from Kushner's previous role as senior adviser to his father-in-law; the full PIF board, headed by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, overruled the panel.
facts.quote: Objections cited by the panel included: the "inexperience" of fund's management; a proposed asset management fee that seemed: "excessive"; and "public relations risks" arising from Kushner's previous role as a senior adviser to his father-in-law.

sources.title: Saudi Arabia: Panel advising sovereign wealth fund objected to $2bn funding of Kushner firm

facts.claim: Senate Finance chairman Ron Wyden's September 24, 2024 letter to Affinity's chief legal officer stated that the PIF's Board Investment Committee had objected to investing in Affinity because of the 'inexperience' of its management and had found Affinity's operations 'unsatisfactory in all aspects', and that the PIF's full board, led by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, overruled the committee and approved the investment. This is a committee letter describing documents, not an official finding.
facts.quote: The investment committee of the Saudi PIF's board of directors objected due to the "inexperience" of Affinity's management, and the Saudi PIF's full board of directors, led by Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman, overruled the investment committee and approved the investment in Affinity.

sources.title: Letter from Chairman Wyden to Chad Mizelle, Chief Legal Officer, Affinity Partners
Wyden Investigation of Kushner Firm Continues; New Letter Outlines Affinity Partners' Fee Structure, Lack of Return to Investors, Questionable Deals with Foreign Governments

facts.claim: Wyden's September 2024 letter stated that Affinity had collected approximately $157.5 million in management fees from foreign investors, including $87 million from the Saudi PIF, and that five other foreign investors, including sovereign wealth funds of Qatar and the UAE and Terry Gou, paid higher rates of 2 percent on the remaining $1 billion committed. Secondary coverage put the PIF fee at 1.25 percent on $2 billion, about $25 million a year. The letter also said Affinity had made no distributions of investment earnings to clients as of July 2024.
facts.quote: Affinity has already collected approximately $157.5 million in management fees from foreign investors, including $87 million from the Saudi PIF. Five other foreign investors, including sovereign wealth funds from Qatar, the United Arab Emirates ("UAE"), and Taiwanese billionaire Terry Gou, are paying even higher rates of 2 percent on the remaining $1 billion committed to Affinity.

sources.title: Letter from Chairman Wyden to Chad Mizelle, Chief Legal Officer, Affinity Partners
Kushner's fund has reaped millions in fees, but so far returned no profits

facts.claim: Affinity disclosed to regulators that about 99 percent of the roughly $3 billion it managed came from non-U.S. persons, according to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission reported by the New York Times and Newsweek.
facts.quote: Affinity has disclosed to regulators that 99 percent of the $3 billion of assets that the firm manages come from non-U.S. persons.

sources.title: Jared Kushner Hit With New Investigation
Jared Kushner's firm received hundreds of millions from UAE, Qatar, says report

facts.claim: The New York Times reported, as relayed by Middle East Eye, that a sovereign wealth fund in the United Arab Emirates invested more than $200 million in Affinity Partners and that an unnamed Qatari entity invested a similar amount.
facts.quote: a sovereign wealth fund in the UAE invested more than $200m in Affinity Partners, while an unnamed Qatari entity invested a similar amount.

sources.title: Jared Kushner's firm received hundreds of millions from UAE, Qatar, says report

facts.claim: In December 2024 Affinity Partners raised an additional $1.5 billion from the Qatar Investment Authority and the Abu Dhabi-based asset manager Lunate, extending the investment period of its debut fund to 2029; a regulatory filing under the name A Fin Management LLC later showed assets under management rose 60 percent in 2024 to $4.8 billion.
facts.quote: Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners raises an additional $1.5 billion from the Qatar Investment Authority and Abu Dhabi-based asset manager Lunate

sources.title: Kushner's Affinity Gets Extra $1.5 Billion From Qatar, Abu Dhabi
Assets at Kushner's Affinity soar after Gulf cash injection

facts.claim: Senator Ron Wyden, as chairman of the Senate Finance Committee, opened an inquiry into Affinity's payments from Gulf governments with a June 12, 2024 letter to the firm's chief financial officer, asking for a list of clients, the amounts each invested and their annual returns, and raising the Foreign Agents Registration Act. Affinity called the inquiry a political move.
facts.quote: Wyden is asking Key to list all of Affinity's clients, how much they've invested, and their annual rates of return.

sources.title: Letter from Chairman Wyden to Lauren Key, Chief Financial Officer, A Fin Management LLC
Senate Democrats launch investigation into Jared Kushner's business

facts.claim: On March 19, 2026, House Oversight ranking member Robert Garcia and Senator Wyden wrote to White House chief of staff Susie Wiles about Kushner's fundraising, stating that Kushner had increased the fees he collects from foreign governments since his father-in-law took office in 2025. The letter is a congressional allegation.
facts.quote: Kushner has already increased the amount of fees he is collecting from foreign governments since his father-in-law took office in 2025.

sources.title: Letter from Ranking Member Garcia and Senator Wyden to White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles

facts.claim: Affinity's reported investments include about $300 million in the Israeli financial group Phoenix Financial and about $110 million in the car-leasing company Shlomo Group; its first announced deal, in July 2022, was in the solar-loan fintech Mosaic. In October 2026 CNN reported on Phoenix's holdings in companies with Israeli military links; Kushner responded that he has no role in deciding what Phoenix buys or sells.
facts.quote: Its investments include about $110 million in car-leasing company Shlomo Group and roughly $300 million in Phoenix Financial.

sources.title: Jared Kushner's Saudi-backed private equity fund clinches first investment in Israel

facts.claim: Affinity's chief legal officer, Chad Mizelle, said the firm had 'early conversations' about fund-raising but 'does not intend to take in any additional capital while Jared is volunteering for the government', after Kushner took on a diplomatic role in the second Trump administration.
facts.quote: Affinity's chief legal officer said the firm had "early conversations" about fund-raising but "does not intend to take in any additional capital while Jared is volunteering for the government."

openQuestions: The PIF screening panel's minutes were reported by the New York Times (unreachable here); the items rely on Middle East Eye's relay and the Senate Finance letters. The owner should open the Senate letters to confirm the exact wording of 'unsatisfactory in all aspects' and which document it quotes.
The UAE sovereign fund that invested in the debut fund is unnamed in the sources reached; no Mubadala connection is recorded.
The $25 million-a-year fee figure is a secondary calculation (1.25 percent of $2 billion); the Senate letter's own figures ($87 million from PIF through mid-2024) are the primary record.
Reported assets under management vary ($4.6 billion, $4.8 billion, $5 billion, 'more than $6 billion' for 2025) by source and date; the Form ADV filing is the primary source.
